kind: Transport replay policy, cached dependency bytecode and four passing real localhost HTTP fixture tests; no user account access or remote health-data writes

scope.target: MiDataClient's default Android/JVM transport for health-cloud POST requests
scope.unchanged_defaults: Passport authentication and FDS clients keep their existing no-argument factory calls and previous default transport behavior.
scope.injected_client: A caller that supplies its own HttpClient must preserve equivalent request-body replay protection when performing writes. The default constructor cannot enforce the behavior of an arbitrary injected client.

dependencies_inspected.inspection_method: Read cached dependency classes using javap -p -c; no library or application code was executed by the static inspection.

static_findings: Ktor 3.6.0 OkHttpConfig's initial builder configuration disables OkHttp followRedirects and followSslRedirects and enables retryOnConnectionFailure. Explicitly retaining disabled engine redirects protects the data-client policy from assumptions about these defaults.
Ktor's implicit redirect policy normally allows GET and HEAD. Disabling Ktor followRedirects for the data client prevents its separate redirect layer from issuing a new call.
OkHttp 5.5.0 RetryAndFollowUpInterceptor.recover checks retryOnConnectionFailure before recovering from a connection exception.
The HTTP 408 branch checks retryOnConnectionFailure, but the HTTP 503 branch can return the original request when Retry-After is zero without checking that setting.

OkHttp's follow-up processing checks a non-null follow-up RequestBody.isOneShot before repeating the request. Marking an already-sent data body one-shot prevents the 503 path from silently sending the POST body again.

android_controls.request_body: For opt-out clients, an application interceptor wraps every non-null RequestBody in NonReplayableRequestBody. It returns true from isOneShot and delegates contentType, contentLength, isDuplex and writeTo to the original body.
android_controls.purpose: A lost upload response must be reconciled with cloud readback rather than an automatic replay below the import runner's journal and conflict checks.

local_fixture_tests.fixture: JDK HttpServer bound to 127.0.0.1 on an ephemeral port, real Ktor/OkHttp client, opaque synthetic bodies, no Xiaomi credentials or health measurements.

cases.expected: The data client returns HTTP 307 and the fixture receives one POST at the original path, with no redirected replay.
The data client does not follow a GET 302; the no-argument default client follows it. This controls for an ineffective redirect fixture and preserves authentication defaults.
After HTTP 503 with Retry-After: 0, the data client sends one POST and returns 503, while the unchanged default-client control sends the body twice and receives the second response.
After a warmup GET, the server consumes a POST body and closes without a response. The data call fails; only one POST body reaches the fixture.

limitations: The local tests exercise the real Android/JVM transport factory over loopback HTTP. They do not perform an encrypted MiDataClient call against Xiaomi, verify live acceptance, or show a record in the official App.
The change blocks automatic POST body replay on the default Android data transport; it is not a guarantee of exactly one HTTP request for an entire synchronization or instrumentation run.
GET requests may still receive native read-only HTTP follow-ups such as 503 handling. Authentication refresh, planned prechecks and later readback requests are also separate from upload replay.
The protection does not prohibit a caller or user from explicitly starting a new request. The import ledger and reconciliation policy remain responsible for deciding whether a later write is safe.
The iOS factory only adapts the shared API and disables Ktor-level redirects. No equivalent NSURLSession connection-recovery or body-replay guarantee has been tested or claimed.
Dependency updates may change follow-up behavior; the loopback regression tests should remain part of the Android/JVM validation gate.
